# Changelog

Changes to OpenBGA Lab Ops, grouped by month and impact.

## November 2026 (2026-11-18 to 2026-11-27)

### High impact

- **Added:** Reveal patient information on one ticket in an emergency (2026-11-27, Tickets)

  Staff you give Can use emergency access can, with a reason, reveal one ticket's patient information for 60 minutes; each use waits for a review by someone else.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `accounts.0013_emergency_access_capability` adds the capability "Can use emergency access" (`use_emergency_access`), granted to nobody, so the feature is off until a superuser gives it to a person or a role group; reversing it deletes the permission with its grants. Migration `desk.0008_emergency_access` adds the tables `desk_emergencyaccess` (one row for each use) and `desk_emergencyreview` (its review), with triggers that refuse `UPDATE` and `DELETE` on both (core's `prevent_record_mutation`) and refuse a review by the person who used the access or of a use whose end has not passed by `transaction_timestamp()`; reversing it is refused once a use is recorded. Migration `audit_review.0006_emergency_access_uses` allows the source `emergency` ("Access review: emergency access") in `audit_review_workspaceuse` (its check constraint is dropped and recreated). None of the three rewrites an existing row. A use lasts 60 minutes, fixed in this release (`desk.emergency.MINUTES`); no new setting or environment variable. Starting a use records the change event `emergency_access.started` (the ticket, the reason code and the times, never the explanation) and a notice under the new outbox topic `desk.emergency` to each supervisor and holder of "Can review access and audit records" with an email address, sent whatever their notice preference; reviewing records `emergency_access.reviewed` (the outcome, never the note). A reveal made under a use adds `emergency` (the use's id) to its `request_form.value_revealed` or `external_link.person_revealed` event. New routes `requests/<id>/emergency/`, `access-review/emergency/` and `access-review/emergency/<id>/`. At its next reset the demonstration seed gives `demo_client_services` the capability, recorded as `account.capability_granted`; the demonstration keeps email off, so its notices are recorded as not sent.

  </details>

- **Security:** The container image installs Debian's published security updates when it is built (2026-11-27)

  The application image now takes Debian's published package updates when it is built, so a security fix is included before the Python base image is rebuilt with it.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  The Dockerfile runs `apt-get update` and `apt-get upgrade` on the `python:3.14.10-slim-bookworm` base before installing the application. This brings in the `libpam` packages `1.5.2-6+deb12u3` from Debian's security archive (CVE-2025-6020, rated High), which the base image did not carry yet. Docker keeps this step in its build cache: an image built again on the same machine reuses the packages of the earlier build. To bring in updates Debian has published since, build without the cache and with a fresh base image (`docker build --pull --no-cache .` from the checkout). A host that builds from a clean cache, as CI does, gets them anyway. No new setting or environment variable.

  </details>

- **Added:** Give a capability or portal access until a last day (2026-11-26, Client organizations)

  Set a last day on a capability given to an account directly, or on a portal account's access; after it, the grant gives nothing.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `accounts.0011_grant_ends` adds the table `accounts_capabilityend` (one end for each account and capability given directly). Migration `clients.0008_grant_ends` adds the nullable column `ends_at` to `clients_portalaccess` and replaces the move trigger function of `clients.0007` so that moving a portal account to another organization also empties its end. Neither changes any data: existing grants have no end and keep holding until someone sets one. Ends are compared with the database's clock (`transaction_timestamp()`) at every check. Setting or moving a capability's end is recorded in the account's `account.updated` event (key `capability_ends`), and a portal access's end in `portal_access.set` and `portal_access.reset` (key `ends_at`, present in every new event of either). At its next reset the demonstration seed gives `demo_supervisor`'s patient-information capability and `demo_client_water`'s site access a last day 90 days later, recorded for the former as `account.capability_end_set`. No new setting or environment variable.

  </details>

- **Added:** Record a signed access review with a keep or remove decision for each grant (2026-11-26, Access review)

  On the new Reviews tab of Access review, decide Keep or Remove for every grant the staff or portal accounts hold, sign with your password, and see which removals are still held.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `audit_review.0005_access_reviews` adds the tables `audit_review_accessreview` and `audit_review_accessreviewitem`, with triggers that refuse `UPDATE` and `DELETE` on both (core's `prevent_record_mutation`), and allows the source `grant_review` ("Access review: reviews") in `audit_review_workspaceuse` (its check constraint is dropped and recreated; no row is rewritten). Reversing it is refused while any access review or a use of the Reviews tab is recorded. Each signing records the change event `access_review.signed`. New routes `access-review/reviews/`, `access-review/reviews/export/`, `access-review/reviews/new/`, `access-review/reviews/<id>/` and `access-review/reviews/<id>/export/`, for staff with a laboratory role who hold "Can review access and audit records". At its next reset the demonstration seed signs one access review of the staff accounts, dated three days before, by `demo_supervisor`, with every grant kept except the Technical staff role of `former_technician`, which is decided for removal and still held. No new setting or environment variable.

  </details>

- **Added:** Record signed reviews of the activity records, and see when the next review is due (2026-11-25, Audit review)

  The new Reviews tab of Audit review keeps a record of each review: the period, what was examined, the findings and follow-up, signed with your password and never changed. It shows when the next review is due at the interval you set and which days no review covers.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `audit_review.0003_review_records` adds the tables `audit_review_review` and `audit_review_reviewnote`, with triggers that refuse `UPDATE` and `DELETE` on both, and `audit_review_reviewschedule`, which holds the review interval in one row written the first time it is saved (none ships). It allows a sixth source, `reviews`, in `audit_review_workspaceuse` (its check constraint is dropped and recreated; no row is rewritten). Reversing it is refused while any review exists, and fails once a use of the Reviews tab is recorded, since workspace use rows cannot be changed or deleted. The Security settings page lists the review interval. A password asked for again, at signing, on any form that asks to confirm it is you or on the re-authentication page (whose form is now `accounts.forms.PasswordReauthenticateForm` in `ACCOUNT_FORMS`), is left out of an error report's request data and of the variables of this application's code that checks it, as are a sign-in's credentials in the account adapter; Django's authentication backend still receives the password as an argument its report filter does not hide (see the operations guide; this release sends no error report). New routes `audit-review/reviews/`, `audit-review/reviews/export/`, `audit-review/reviews/new/`, `audit-review/reviews/interval/`, `audit-review/reviews/<id>/` and `audit-review/reviews/<id>/note/`. No new setting or environment variable.

  </details>

- **Added:** Confirm it is you before changing access or security settings (2026-11-24, Security settings)

  Saving a change to accounts, roles, session limits or the second-factor rule asks for your password again, and your authenticator code if you have one (an account without a password gives the code alone).

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  No migration and no new setting. The 5 minutes follow `ACCOUNT_REAUTHENTICATION_TIMEOUT`, and a confirmation is recorded in the browser's session as allauth records a re-authentication, so allauth's own re-authentication pages count toward it and it counts for them; signing in does not count. A password given counts only while the account keeps the password that was checked (the session keeps a keyed digest of its stored hash, never the password), and a code only while the account keeps the authenticator it came from and when it was given after the newest authenticator app was added, so a new password or a new or replaced app asks again. It asks on the admin console's Add user, an account's page, its password page, Mark as compromised, removing an authenticator, Add group and a group's page, and on the staff and client portal session limits and the second-factor rule forms on Security settings. A password or code not accepted is written to the person's sign-in history as a failed re-authentication and counts toward the failed sign-in limit; nothing typed is stored, logged or written to an audit event or the admin console's history, and every request marks the two fields as sensitive, so a Django error report never shows them. A password change refused in the admin console (both buttons sent, as without script) no longer writes a password-changed audit event, and removing an authenticator keeps the admin console's popup. An account with neither a usable password nor an authenticator cannot make these changes. Ending an account's sessions does not ask. Security settings lists the rule under Sign-in as Changing access and security settings.

  </details>

- **Added:** Confirm it is you before revealing patient information (2026-11-24, Security settings)

  Administrators can ask staff to confirm it is them (their password and, where they have an authenticator app, a code from it or a recovery code; an account without a password gives the code alone) before their first reveal of patient information in each session.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `core` 0008 adds the `RevealConfirmationRule` table. Its one row is written only when an administrator first saves the setting on Security settings, so an upgraded or new database asks nothing until then. When it is on, the first Reveal of a patient-information value or Reveal key of a person-level link in a browser session goes to the new Confirm it is you page (`/account/confirm-reveal/`); nothing is read, revealed or recorded until the person confirms, and they then choose Reveal again. The confirmation is kept in the session under `_reveal_confirmed`, naming the account and the sign-in's session row (`_account_session`), so it lasts for that sign-in only: a sign-out clears it, and a new sign-in, even of the same account in the same browser, asks again. A confirmation given in that sign-in within `ACCOUNT_REAUTHENTICATION_TIMEOUT` (5 minutes) for another change, or on allauth's own re-authentication pages with every factor the account has, counts and is remembered for the sign-in, and opening the confirmation page then returns straight to the page without asking; the sign-in itself does not count. Failed confirmations are written to the sign-in history and count toward the failed sign-in limit. Staff without the patient-information permission who post to a reveal address are asked first, then refused as before (404). Not asked before a person-level key search or for what client portal accounts see. Changes to the setting need a reason and the person's confirmation, and are recorded as `lab.reveal_confirmation_changed` in the Security settings history.

  </details>

- **Added:** Review access and audit records across the laboratory (2026-11-24, Audit review)

  Holders of the new capability "Can review access and audit records" filter and export every change, access record and sign-in in Audit review; each use is recorded.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  New capability `accounts.review_audit_records` ("Can review access and audit records"), granted to nobody; a superuser grants it in the admin console to a person or a role group, and it takes effect for a staff account with a laboratory role. Migrations: `accounts.0010_review_capability` (the capability and an index on `accounts_signinevent (occurred_at DESC)`), `core.0010_recent_history_indexes` (indexes on `core_auditevent` and `core_accessrecord (occurred_at DESC)`) and `audit_review.0001_initial` (the table `audit_review_workspaceuse`, with check constraints and a trigger that refuses `UPDATE` and `DELETE`). While each index is built, writes to its table wait: seconds for the rows a laboratory keeps; plan the upgrade outside busy hours if those tables hold millions of rows. A workspace use row is written for each page of the workspace shown and each export, with the account id, the list, the filters accepted (ids, codes and dates), the rows matched and the request ID, before the page or file is sent; if it cannot be written, the request fails with a server error. Exports are CSV files of at most 10,000 rows, built in memory. No new setting or environment variable. New routes under `audit-review/` (`changes/`, `access/`, `sign-ins/`, `uses/` and an `export/` of each) and the remote option list `lookups/review-accounts/`. The public demonstration grants the capability to `demo_supervisor` from its next daily reset. Reversing the migrations deletes the workspace use records, the three indexes and the capability with its grants to people and groups.

  </details>

- **Added:** See who opened a ticket (2026-11-24, Tickets)

  Opening a ticket, its form details or complaint forms, downloading a file and being shown a patient-marked answer are now recorded; supervisors read them under More, Who opened it.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `core.0009_access_records` adds the table `core_accessrecord`, with check constraints and a trigger that refuses `UPDATE` and `DELETE`, and the column `core_auditevent.request_ref` (blank by database default, so a release still running during the upgrade keeps recording change events; events from before the upgrade, and from scheduled jobs and commands, have no request ID). An access record is written for each staff or client portal ticket page drawn (also after a refused reply, note or contact), audit history, Who opened it, Form details and complaint form page, file download, staff reveal of a patient-marked answer or a person-level key (besides its change event), patient-marked answer shown on a portal ticket page, new ticket opened with Request again (for the ticket its answers come from) and ticket whose entries a client organization's timeline page shows. It holds the account id, the capacity (laboratory staff or client portal), the kind, the ticket id, the file, answer or link id and the request ID that the `lab_ops.request` log line and the `X-Request-ID` header carry; never a subject, text, answer, file name, key or content. A refused read, a HEAD request and an answer another layer put in place of the page record nothing; if the record cannot be written, the request fails with a server error and the page is not sent. A process of the new release records from the moment the migration has applied; records are complete once no process of the earlier release serves requests. They are kept with no retention period and grow by about one row per page view, plus one per patient-marked answer on a portal ticket page and one per ticket shown on a client timeline page (up to 25). Lists and searches are not recorded. Reversing the migration deletes the records and the change events' request IDs. No new setting or environment variable. New route: `requests/<id>/access/` (supervisors).

  </details>

- **Changed:** Longer passwords, checked against common and expected ones (2026-11-23, Security settings)

  New passwords need 15 characters, or 8 where a second sign-in factor is required; each password form says which, and common or predictable ones are refused.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  `AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS` is now `accounts.passwords.LengthByFactorValidator`, `accounts.passwords.AccountSimilarityValidator` (Django's similarity check against the account as it stands), Django's `CommonPasswordValidator` and `accounts.passwords.ExpectedPasswordValidator`; Django's `MinimumLengthValidator` and `NumericPasswordValidator` are no longer used, so no rule asks for particular kinds of character. Existing passwords keep working and meet the rule when next changed. `ACCOUNT_FORMS` points allauth's change, set and reset-from-link password forms at `accounts.forms`, which state the rule for their account. `seed_demo` now needs `DEMO_PASSWORD` and `DEMO_ADMIN_PASSWORD` of at least 15 characters (was 12) that meet the rule for each account it creates: set such ones before the next demonstration reset. `manage.py changepassword` now saves the password alone. `ACCOUNT_PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_GENERATOR` is `accounts.tokens.ResetTokenGenerator`: a reset link does not work while its account is a shared demonstration account; other links are unchanged.

  </details>

- **Added:** Mark a password as compromised, so the person must choose a new one (2026-11-23, Security settings)

  A superuser marks a password someone else may know as compromised from the account's page in the admin console, with a reason: the account's sessions end, the password alone no longer signs in, and a sign-in that also gives an authenticator code or an emailed code opens only Choose a new password.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `accounts.0008_compromised_password` adds the `CompromisedPassword` table (one open mark per account, kept after it is lifted, with a copy of the marked password's stored hash) and the `password_compromised` session ending. `MIDDLEWARE` gains `accounts.compromised.PasswordChangeMiddleware` after `accounts.enrolment.EnrolmentMiddleware`, and `AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS` gains `accounts.passwords.MarkedPasswordValidator`, which refuses a password marked for the account. Any new password lifts the mark: on Choose a new password (`/account/new-password/`), through an emailed reset link, or set on the account's password page in the admin console; a hash Django upgrades at sign-in does not. A sign-in that proves only the password starts its session ended; one that also proves a second factor or an emailed code sets up a second factor first where the laboratory requires one, then chooses a new password. Nothing is emailed to the person. Marks are enforced and lifted only by processes running this release: mark passwords once the deployment has finished, and check open marks after a rollback; reversing the migration deletes the marks. `PASSWORD_HASHERS` is now one of the settings Security settings compares with this release. Marking is recorded as `account.password_marked_compromised` and the new password chosen on that page as `account.password_changed`, without the password or its hash.

  </details>

- **Added:** Require a second sign-in factor (2026-11-23, Security settings)

  Administrators choose which accounts must use an authenticator app; those accounts set one up at their next sign-in, before anything else.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `core.0006_second_factor_rule` adds the rule's table (one row, written the first time an administrator saves it, so nothing is required until then); `accounts.0007_accountsession_second_factor_required` adds a column with a database default to each session, recording whether the rule covered the account at sign-in. A new middleware, `accounts.enrolment.EnrolmentMiddleware`, follows `accounts.sessions.SessionLimitMiddleware`: a session the rule covered whose account has no authenticator app reaches only `/account/second-factor/`, the two-factor setup and re-authentication pages, sign-in, Sign out and the session status addresses. Sessions the rule did not cover at sign-in are not interrupted when it changes. The account and the rule are read together in one statement. `MFA_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_EMAIL` is now on: sign-up is closed, and allauth's check against unverified addresses would leave a required account without outgoing email unable to add an authenticator.

  </details>

- **Added:** See your sign-in history (2026-11-23)

  Sign-in history, in the account menu, lists your sign-ins, sign-outs and failed or refused attempts of the last 90 days, so you can spot any you do not recognize.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `accounts.0009_sign_in_history` adds the table `accounts_signinevent`, the column `accounts_accountsession.factor` (blank by database default, so a release still running during the upgrade keeps signing people in; its sign-ins show the factor as not recorded) and triggers: the database writes each session's sign-in and sign-out to the history, and refuses `UPDATE` and `DELETE` on it, so entries are append-only. At sign-in, a wrong password, or one the failed sign-in limit refused, is recorded only for the one account the username or email address names; on re-authentication or Change password, for the signed-in account; a wrong code, and a refusal at the code step, for the account already identified at that step; a refused sign-in for the account whose password or code was accepted; refusals by the limit at most once a minute for each account, step and address; no entry holds a password, a code or a typed identifier. A sign-in completing after its account was deactivated now starts its session ended. History starts at the upgrade, entries are kept with no retention period, also when an account is deleted by means other than the application (which deactivates accounts). Reversing the migration deletes the history. The address follows `ALLAUTH_TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT` or `ALLAUTH_TRUSTED_CLIENT_IP_HEADER`, as for sessions. No new setting. The sign-in log (`lab_ops.signin`) gains a `signout.deactivated` line for a sign-in whose session starts ended because its account was deactivated while it was under way.

  </details>

- **Added:** Get back what you were typing after a sign-out (2026-11-22)

  When a session limit signs you out, what you were typing in a ticket's reply or note, a portal reply or a new portal ticket comes back when you sign in again in the same browser.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `accounts.0005_kept_draft` adds the table of kept typing and one row per account for the moment it last used Sign out. A copy is stored only after its session ended by a limit, for that account and the browser that sent it, identified by the SHA-256 of a random value in a new HttpOnly cookie, `lab_ops_kept` (Secure as the session cookie is, SameSite=Lax, 24 hours, set with each page that draws a kept form); files and fields that hold patient information are never kept. It is drawn back into the form on the server, given back once, discarded at Sign out, never logged or audited, and removed 24 hours after the sign-out by a new scheduled job, `remove_kept_typing`; without a scheduler, copies are no longer given back after 24 hours but stay in the database until a run removes it. A Sign out handled by the previous release while this one rolls out does not remove copies, but they are not given back afterwards. The page sends the copy to `account/session/keep/`, which takes no CSRF token: a token signed for the form's account and session stands in for it. A GET of the address a refused reply is drawn at (`/requests/<id>/entries/`, `/portal/requests/<number>/reply/`) now opens the ticket instead of answering 405.

  </details>

- **Security:** See where you are signed in and sign out elsewhere (2026-11-21)

  Where you are signed in, in the account menu, lists your open sessions with their browser and address and signs out the ones you no longer use. A superuser can end a person's sessions from the admin console, with a reason.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `accounts.0004_session_browser_address` adds the browser (`User-Agent`, up to 300 characters, with a database default so a release still running during the upgrade keeps signing people in) and the client address at sign-in to each session; existing sessions show neither. The address follows `ALLAUTH_TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT` or `ALLAUTH_TRUSTED_CLIENT_IP_HEADER`, as the sign-in limits do: behind a proxy without either, every session shows the proxy's address. The sign-in log (`lab_ops.signin`) adds `signout.signed_out_elsewhere` and `signout.administrator`, and each ending is an `account.sessions_ended` audit event without browsers or addresses. A session that has passed a session limit when it is ended, by any of these, a deactivation or a new password, is now recorded as ended by that limit, at the moment the limit passed.

  </details>

- **Security:** Sign out after a period without activity (2026-11-21, Security settings)

  Sessions are signed out after a period without activity and after a longest session, which administrators set on Security settings for staff and for client portal accounts. Pages warn before signing out and offer Stay signed in, and signing in again returns to the page. Deactivating an account or setting a new password ends its other sessions at once, and pages are no longer kept by the browser.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migrations `accounts.0003_account_session` and `core.0005_sessionlimit` add a table of sessions (start, last activity, end and why) and a table of session limits. Neither writes rows: limits never saved are 30 minutes without activity and 12 hours at most, set from 5 to 60 minutes and 1 to 24 hours. After the upgrade, everyone signed in is asked to sign in once more, because sessions from earlier releases carry no session record. `SESSION_COOKIE_AGE` is now 24 hours, the longest a session can last, counted by the cookie from when the session was last saved. The new `accounts.sessions.SessionLimitMiddleware` follows the message middleware, and the new `accounts.sessions.NoStoreMiddleware`, first in `MIDDLEWARE`, marks every answer to a signed-in session `Cache-Control: no-store`; the laboratory's logo keeps its caching. The sign-in log (`lab_ops.signin`) adds `signout.inactivity`, `signout.maximum`, `signout.deactivated` and `signout.new_password`.

  </details>

- **Added:** OpenBGA Lab Ops initial release (2026-11-18)

  Staff can manage client organizations, assign tickets and track service deadlines. Clients can request service, send attachments and follow replies in their portal.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  For a local trial, start the Docker Compose app profile and run seed_demo. For a laboratory installation, configure PostgreSQL, run the migrations and use setup_lab to create the laboratory and its first administrator.

  </details>

- **Added:** Record nonconformances and corrective actions (2026-11-18, Nonconformances, [#4](https://github.com/openbga/lab-ops/pull/4))

  Track a problem from containment to an effectiveness check, with dated actions and closing by another supervisor. Administrators switch the module on in the laboratory profile.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migrations `core.0003_labmodule` and `nonconformance.0001_initial` add the module switch and the new tables. Every optional module starts switched off, so an upgraded laboratory sees no change until an administrator switches it on. The demonstration seed switches it on and adds four synthetic records at its next reset.

  </details>

- **Added:** Retry email notices and run scheduled jobs (2026-11-18, Scheduled jobs)

  Notices the mail server refuses are retried. Teams hear when a ticket passes a service target, and resolved tickets can close after a set number of days.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Run `python manage.py run_scheduled_jobs` every five minutes from the host's scheduler, with the web service's image, database and mail settings (see docs/operations.md, "Scheduled jobs"). Without it, notices are still sent once after each change, but nothing is retried or closed automatically. Migrations add the `jobs` app's tables and two columns to ticket clocks; clocks already past their target at upgrade are marked as noticed so the first run does not notify old breaches. Notices are now recorded before sending: with the dummy mail backend they are recorded as not sent and never sent later. New setting `EMAIL_TIMEOUT` (seconds, default 10) bounds each wait for the mail server.

  </details>

- **Added:** Review security settings and name security contacts (2026-11-18, Security settings)

  Administrators see what protects sign-in, sessions and patient information, and record the laboratory's security and privacy contacts with a reason.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `core.0004_labcontact` adds the contacts table. It writes no rows: a contact exists once an administrator records it. The Security settings page reads the deployment's settings and changes none of them. The demonstration seed records two invented contacts at its next reset. The new `docs/safeguards.md` states what the application does for each safeguard the roadmap cites. A blank `CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY` now sends no header instead of an empty one, and whitespace in the policy is sent as single spaces. The refusal of a form whose CSRF check failed is marked not to be stored.

  </details>

### Medium impact

- **Added:** See what an account held when it was deactivated (2026-11-27, Accounts & roles)

  Deactivate an account with a reason after seeing what it holds; its page then keeps what it held, who deactivated it and when.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `accounts.0012_deactivation` adds the table `accounts_deactivation`, with a trigger that refuses `UPDATE` and `DELETE` on it. It changes no data: no record is written for an account deactivated before it, and such an account's page says that what it held then was not recorded. From this release, every save of an account that deactivates it (the new Deactivate page, clearing Active on the account's page, or code that saves the account) writes one record in the same transaction; a change made with `QuerySet.update` or raw SQL writes none. The Deactivate page (`admin/accounts/user/<id>/deactivate/`, route `admin:accounts_user_deactivate`) is for active superusers with staff status, asks them to confirm it is them, and records the change event `account.updated` with the reason. Reversing the migration drops the table and its records. No new setting or environment variable.

  </details>

- **Added:** Count what each person did, and what happened outside business hours, in Audit review (2026-11-25, Audit review)

  The new People tab of Audit review counts, for each person over a period, their sign-ins, failed or refused sign-ins, tickets opened, files downloaded, patient information shown and changes made, and how many of these happened outside the hours of one of your business calendars. Select a count to open the rows behind it. Changes, Access records and Sign-ins can now be narrowed to what happened outside a business calendar's hours.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `audit_review.0002_people_summary` allows a fifth source, `people`, in `audit_review_workspaceuse` (its check constraint is dropped and recreated in one transaction; no row is rewritten). Reversing it fails once a use of the People tab is recorded, since workspace use rows cannot be changed or deleted. New routes `audit-review/people/` and `audit-review/people/export/`. Business hours come from the active business calendars the service clocks use, read as they stand when a page is drawn; a period judged against one covers at most 366 days. No new setting or environment variable.

  </details>

- **Added:** See every account's roles and capabilities with who gave them, and list accounts nobody has used (2026-11-25, Access review)

  The new Access review, under Oversight, lists every account with its roles, capabilities, teams, portal access, second factor and last sign-in, and who gave each role, capability and admin console access and when. A second tab lists the active accounts with no sign-in for a period the laboratory sets.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `audit_review.0004_access_report` adds the table `audit_review_unusedperiod`, which holds the unused account period in one row written the first time it is saved (none ships), and allows two more sources, `accounts` and `unused`, in `audit_review_workspaceuse` (its check constraint is dropped and recreated; no row is rewritten). Reversing it fails once a use of Access review is recorded, since workspace use rows cannot be changed or deleted. New routes `access-review/accounts/`, `access-review/accounts/export/`, `access-review/unused/`, `access-review/unused/export/` and `access-review/unused/period/`, for staff with a laboratory role who hold "Can review access and audit records". At its next reset the demonstration seed sets the unused account period to 90 days, adds the synthetic staff account `former_technician`, which has no password and last signed in 120 days before, and records a change event naming the role of each demonstration staff account it creates. Two saves of a role group's page at once, or a role group renamed while an account naming it is saved, now record each grant once and under the name the group had when it was recorded: the role group page holds the group's row before it reads the values it records, and the account pages and `setup_lab` read the role names as they record the change. No new setting or environment variable.

  </details>

- **Added:** Email notices when your sign-in factors change (2026-11-24)

  You are emailed when your authenticator app or recovery codes change, or a superuser marks your password as compromised, so you notice a change you did not make.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  No migration and no new setting. The notices go through the existing outbox under the topic `accounts.security` and are retried by `run_scheduled_jobs`; with email off, as on the public demonstration, they are recorded as Not sent. They are sent when a superuser marks a password as compromised or removes an authenticator app or recovery codes in the admin console, and when the person adds an authenticator app (one notice, which mentions new recovery codes when the app was added with new ones; allauth issues them only when the account has none), generates new recovery codes or removes the app on their own two-factor pages. Each names the laboratory, the username, what changed and when (UTC), and the laboratory's security contact from its profile (or "your laboratory's administrator"), with no code, secret, network address, browser or ticket content, and links only to the site's address. They are sent whatever the person chose on Email notices, and not when the account is inactive or has no email address when sent. A password changed by the person or set by a superuser, and an email address change, send no notice. allauth's three two-factor pages that change factors (`mfa_activate_totp`, `mfa_generate_recovery_codes`, `mfa_deactivate_totp`) are now served by `accounts.mfa_views` at the same paths and URL names, included before allauth's URLs; they run allauth's own flow in one transaction that locks the account and also records `account.authenticator_added`, `account.recovery_codes_replaced` or `account.authenticator_removed` audit events with factor ids, types and times only. allauth's own `ACCOUNT_EMAIL_NOTIFICATIONS` is left at its default, off. Scheduled jobs lists a failed or retrying one as an Account notice without saying whose account it is.

  </details>

- **Security:** Failed sign-ins count the same in every server process (2026-11-23, Security settings)

  The limit on failed sign-ins now counts attempts together across all of the deployment's server processes, rather than in each one.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  `CACHES` is now `core.cache.SharedCache`, Django's database cache in the table `lab_ops_cache`, created by migration `core.0007_shared_cache_table` (run `migrate`; `createcachetable` is not needed). Keys are stored as HMACs made with `SECRET_KEY` (`core.cache.keyed_digest`), so the table holds no name or address; rotating `SECRET_KEY` starts the counts afresh. Every write removes expired entries, a live one is never removed to make room, and an entry lasts at least as long as asked. A deployment that replaces `CACHES` with a per-process cache gives each worker its own counts again, and Security settings says the configuration changed.

  </details>

- **Added:** Get back a new ticket you were typing after a sign-out (2026-11-22, Tickets)

  When a session limit signs you out while you log a ticket, what you typed comes back on New ticket when you sign in again in the same browser, with its category, organization, site, contact and ticket form. This works when you were typing in the dialog over the ticket list too.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  No migration. The new ticket keeps its own fields, the ticket form chosen and that form's fields as one copy under the form key `staff-ticket`, in the table and with the cookie added by the previous release. The organization, site and contact are kept by id and given back only while still active. Files and fields that hold patient information are never kept. When a copy is held for a form in the shared form dialog, signing in again returns to that form's own address instead of the page behind the dialog.

  </details>

- **Added:** Get back nonconformance typing after a sign-out (2026-11-22, Quality)

  When a session limit signs you out while you work a nonconformance or its actions, what you typed comes back on that form when you sign in again. If the record changed meanwhile, saving is refused.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `accounts.0006_kept_draft_revision` adds a nullable `revision` column to the kept-typing table; a release still running while it applies goes on inserting rows without it. Each nonconformance form keeps its copy under a key naming the form and the record, with the revision the form posts: the page that gives it back posts that revision, so a save is checked against the record as it stood when the person typed. A form page opened with GET is drawn in one reading and leaves the copy in place when it is not drawn after all.

  </details>

- **Fixed:** Saves check what changed while they waited (2026-11-20)

  Saves now decide from records as they stand: an account page opened earlier cannot undo a newer change, and a portal reply refused on a closed ticket is shown again.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  No migration or setting. On the account administration page, Last login and Date joined are now read only, and a save writes only the fields the page edits. A password change, by the person or on the account's password page, saves only the password.

  </details>

- **Fixed:** Clarify account recovery and email availability (2026-11-18)

  Account pages explain email availability, verification and recovery codes. Keyboard users can read and dismiss phone Help without losing their place.

- **Fixed:** Clarify ticket replies and changes (2026-11-18, Tickets)

  Replies identify their portal audience, closed tickets offer internal notes, and ticket history shows the values changed by staff.

- **Fixed:** Edit and reorder ticket forms (2026-11-18)

  Field settings follow the selected type, preset comparisons show their counts, and moving a form keeps it in view.

- **Fixed:** Find client tickets and services (2026-11-18, Client organizations)

  Organizations link to all their open tickets. Portal ticket entry points offer the same services and select a client's sole available site.

- **Fixed:** Keep your place in ticket queues (2026-11-18, Tickets)

  Clearing a search keeps the current view. Staff can correct a bulk action with its selection intact and confirm a saved view's deletion.

- **Fixed:** Protect ticket drafts and file selections (2026-11-18, Tickets)

  Ticket actions protect an unfinished entry. After a form error, choose missing files again or explicitly leave them out before submitting.

- **Changed:** Read ticket details and conversations together (2026-11-18, Tickets)

  Staff can read the latest conversation below the ticket details and use Add entry to reply, write a note or log a call.

- **Changed:** Scan work queues and recent organizations (2026-11-18, Dashboard)

  The dashboard shows each queue's count and oldest ticket in a compact row, with recent organizations alongside on wider screens.

### Low impact

- **Fixed:** A ticket's way back to the queue keeps your latest list settings (2026-11-21, Tickets)

  Going back to Tickets from a ticket or its action pages, after changing several tickets, or from Save view's own page, now sends only the filters, sort and rows per page you chose on the list. A sort or rows per page you did not choose there follows your saved settings as they are then, including a change made in another tab (in a saved view, its own order), and searching or filtering no longer sets them aside. Previous in list and Next in list now also appear when you open a ticket from the list without choosing a filter or sort. A view saved from the list keeps the order it showed, even the default order, and opening a saved view no longer changes your own saved sort (a link to a view saved earlier still carries its sort). From now on, a saved view's history records that it keeps a search, not the search text; entries recorded earlier are unchanged. The Awaiting review filter now shows complaints only to supervisors, who are the ones who can review them.

- **Fixed:** File lists and the ticket composer show their intended layout (2026-11-21, Tickets)

  Chosen files and a ticket entry's files are listed with their spacing again, a withdrawn file is struck through, and the composer no longer offers files for a logged contact. A missing brace in the style sheet had switched those styles off in current browsers.

- **Fixed:** Deactivations and organization changes wait their turn (2026-11-20)

  Deactivating a ticket's assignee while a client replies, and changing organizations or site codes during an import, now wait for each other instead of one failing.

- **Changed:** Link changes count as ticket changes (2026-11-20, Tickets)

  Adding, removing, showing or hiding a ticket's link now counts as a change to the ticket: a reply, note or link change sent from a page opened before it is refused.

- **Fixed:** Saved layouts and What's new visits show in every tab (2026-11-20)

  A column layout, page size, sidebar choice or What's new visit made in one tab or workstation shows on the next page in the others.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  No migration. Each request reads the person's preferences from the database once; nothing is copied into the session any more, so two tabs answering at the same moment can no longer put back an older value, such as a What's new mark. A list's page size and sort, and the What's new mark, are combined with the value stored when saving, so another tab's choice is kept; a list saves only the page size and sort it applied with valid filters, once the page is ready, so an old link's sort, refused filters, an error or a lookup save nothing, and a list's links and forms (Rows per page, Next, a sort heading, Apply) no longer send back a sort or page size saved earlier. A display setting that is refused or may not have been saved shows a notice. The client timeline no longer offers a Rows per page control it did not apply. Sessions signed in earlier keep an unused copy until they end.

  Adding a preference counts the person's preferences and inserts holding a transaction-level advisory lock (keys 19557 and the account's id modulo 2,147,483,647), so the limit of 300 holds when two are added at once. A list page opened at the limit with a page size or sort in its address now follows it without saving it, instead of failing with a server error.

  While a deploy replaces processes one by one, processes of the earlier release still read and write their session copy and add preferences without the lock, so until every process runs this release a page they serve can show an older value, and the limit can be passed by as many preferences as those processes add at that moment.

  Changing a display preference no longer saves the session, so it no longer extends its length (Security settings, Session length).

  </details>

- **Fixed:** Ticket pages agree with the replies they show (2026-11-20)

  A ticket opened while someone replies shows that reply only with forms that accept your answer to it, on the desk and in the portal.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  The scheduled jobs' account, when a deployment's first job run creates it, is now named `scheduled-jobs-` followed by eight random characters, with the matching address in the reserved `lab-ops.invalid` domain, so a person's account registered at that moment under the old name does not delay it or end up differing from it only in letter case. An account created earlier keeps its name.

  The ticket reply and entry posts now run outside any request transaction, also where a deployment turns `ATOMIC_REQUESTS` on; their services open their own.

  </details>

- **Fixed:** Assigning while someone's access ends (2026-11-19, Tickets)

  An assignment and the assignee's deactivation or removal from the team at the same moment now wait for each other instead of failing with an error. A change saved while a colleague recategorizes the ticket is refused as changed, keeping what you typed, instead of showing the ticket as missing.

- **Fixed:** Ending someone's access while they save (2026-11-19, Tickets)

  Deactivating a person, or removing a role, capability, team or portal site, now waits for a change they are saving, and anything they start afterwards is refused. Importing external identifiers no longer fails with an error when someone adds a link at the same moment.

- **Added:** Security checks on every change (2026-11-19)

  Each change is checked for vulnerable components, committed secrets and unsafe code, and each release lists its components.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Pull requests and a weekly run on `main` go through CodeQL static analysis of the Python code, the
  JavaScript under `static/js/` and the workflows; a Grype audit of `uv.lock`, the vendored browser
  packages and the workflows' actions; a gitleaks scan of the history, which also runs on every push;
  and a Grype scan of the container image. Before trusting a clean result, each check compares its listing with what it must
  contain and runs its settings against a known finding. Each run keeps a software bill of materials
  of the image (SPDX 2.3 and CycloneDX 1.6) for 90 days, and each release published on GitHub
  carries it as release assets. The security policy (`SECURITY.md`) lists what fails each check and
  what is not checked. The vendored browser packages are now also recorded in
  `static/vendor/package-lock.json`, which is served with the other static files. Nothing is
  installed from it, and deployments need no change.

  </details>

- **Fixed:** Steadier email notices after a save (2026-11-19, Scheduled jobs)

  A save that changes several tickets waits for a slow mail server once and stops at its first refusal. The Scheduled jobs account no longer offers Set password.

- **Changed:** Give the ticket subject a full-width heading (2026-11-18, Tickets)

  Staff tickets show the number and subject in a smaller heading above the status and actions, leaving more room for the conversation and details.
